options.text: Guard cells alone, without any pores.
Stomata only on the lower surface of leaves.

stem:
Myra holds a leaf from the school garden. She names stomata, guard cells, chloroplasts, and xylem tubes. During photosynthesis the leaf exchanges carbon dioxide and oxygen.

Which structures help that gas exchange?

teacher.key_rationale: Stomata are the tiny pores on leaf surfaces that help exchange carbon dioxide and oxygen; guard cells regulate them, chloroplasts run photosynthesis, and stomata are not limited to the lower surface only in this hinge.
